recipes.name: Classic Slow Cooker Corn Chowder
ingredients_raw: 2 (10.75 ounce) cans condensed cream of mushroom soup
2 cups frozen shredded hash brown potatoes
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Stir milk, cream-style corn, cream of mushroom soup, chopped green chiles, frozen corn, hash brown potatoes, ham, onion, butter, hot sauce, parsley, and chili powder in a slow cooker. Season with salt and black pepper. Cover and cook on High for 4 hours or on Low and for 6 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Classic Slow Cooker Corn Chowder
raw_recipe.description: A comforting and creamy corn chowder with potatoes and ham is made in the slow cooker. Chili powder and hot sauce adds a little kick.

video.description: It may be summertime, but you need to bust out the slow cooker ASAP. In this video, Nicole teaches you how to make a corn chowder recipe so easy and convenient, dinner won’t be a worry ever again. Cream of mushroom and chopped ham give this chowder a salty taste, but the sweet corn and tender potatoes round out this meal in a savory and refreshing way. Chopped green chiles give an extra kick of flavor, making this corn chowder a fan-favorite.

review.reviewBody:
I loved it! I can't wait to used this recipe and and lots of different items. Carrots, celery, etc... Thanks for the recipe!

Oh and by the way. I made it exactly as written. I think it's wrong to change a recipe and then rate it. :( How is that a fair rating?????

My husband and I loved this chowder. I did make a few changes. I used 1 can of cream of mushroom soup, 1 can of chiles, 1 can regular corn instead of frozen, 1 tablespoon hot sauce and a little more that 1/2 teaspoon of chili powder. I also added about 1.5 cups of chedar cheese. Otherwise, I followed the recipe. I also served the chowder in bread bowls. It was YUMMY!!

I made this recipe many times , I have made changes to it though, 1) I used 2 cans cream of celery soup. cream of mushroom soup just doesn't go with all the other ingredients. 2) I used 2 cups cream & 1 cup milk. 3 cups milk is way to watery. cream is also sweeter and adds a nice thickness to the chowder. 3) no chile's were added , I'm from new England and chile's are original to the way chowder should be . 4) 2 cans of corn used instead of frozen. 5) 2 large russet potatoes used diced small. 5) 1/2 Vidalia onion used diced. 

I find these changes make for an excellent chowder that's closer to the original from New England.

I admit I made a couple changes, but this recipe turned out awesome! I only used 1 can green chili's, used 1- 12 oz can evaporated milk and water to make up the rest of the liquid, after reading other reviews, I omitted the hot sauce since my man doesn't like super spicy and I used 5 real potatoes diced up. If I would have had more time I would cook it on low for probably 8 hours since I used regular potatoes but I did it on high for 4 and low for 2 and it tastes awesome! I did add a little velvetta I had in the fridge too. I'm so glad I found this recipe! Lunch this week is going to be tasty! Thanks Michelle!

I changed a few items. Omitted green chiles because family doesn't like them. Used crm of mushroom and crm of chicken soup because it was what I had on hand. Cooked on high for 4-5 hrs. Onion was still a bit crunchy. Next time I will saute the onion in the butter before mixing and possibly add bacon for additional flavor. Also, I will cook on low for 4-6 hrs so the potatoes don't overcook. The flavor was very good! - lsragan

Wow!! Great recipe! I used one can cream of chicken and one of mushroom because i had those on hand. I used 2 cans of evaporated milk because i didn't want to use fresh milk. I used cumin instead of chili powder and omitted the hot sauce. I added diced carrots and 3 slices of pepper jack cheese. I did use only one can of regular corn instead of frozen because i was out of frozen. Very yummy.

Though I did alter it a bit, this is an outstanding recipe. I have used 1/2c crumbled bacon in place of the ham. I've also added diced carrot and celery. In place of one of the mushroom soups, I have used Cream of Celery. Chipotle's corn salsa is terrific for the 2c corn. One final touch is to add some shredded Kale in the last hour of cooking. I don't do all of these every time, but it seems that you can't go wrong with this recipe!

This was really good! Did not add the hot sauce and it still had a little bite. Simmered on the stovetop in a Dutch oven, uncovered for about 1 1/2 hours. Used Southern style hash browns (little cubes) and it worked fine.
So easy to add cooked shrimp or scallops to a bowl and then pour it on top. Easy, but elegant.

I loved this recipe. However I didn’t use a slow cooker as I didn’t have time. I cooked it in my stock pot on the stove. I also just diced up potatoes to use since I didn’t have frozen hash browns. I diced them small to cook faster. I also doubled the recipe as I have a large family. 
We loved it and I’m about to make it again even though it’s 90 degrees outside! This time I’ll make sure to use a smoked ham as I think this will make it even better.

I took it to a church function and it was all the rave! I added a jar of chopped up roasted bell peppers and used cream of chicken and cream of celery soup instead of the cream of mushroom since I don't like mushrooms.
Luv it but sub 2 cup of cream & 1 cup of milk. So creamy & delicious. This is on repeat!!!!
Perfect for an easy home cooked delicious meal. Serve with crusty bread and you will want to make this soup again, and again!
My husband has 3 bowls- that says a lot. I loved the flavor and how easy it was. I recommend this highly!

This recipe does not fit in a standard size slow cooker, as I found out the very hard way. It's perfectly reasonable for a recipe to require a larger slow cooker, but please state that so people don't waste a bunch of money trying something they can't actually cook.
made exactly, just 1 can of chopped peppers. really good. no hot sauce. just enough of a kick for me.
I added some chopped celery with the onion.
I made this over the weekend. I've never made corn chowder before so nothing to compare it to; however, it was flavorful and filling.
I followed the recipe as written, and my husband and I both loved it. The spices and hot sauce really gave it some oomph!
